title: Commit-window planner and oncall routing for dedicated reservations
creator: Maya Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines the provisioning lifecycle pieces required to safely accept, schedule, and operate Dedicated capacity reservations that carry throughput guarantees. It bundles two tightly-coupled capabilities: (1) a commit-window planner and sizing concierge that computes safe provisioning windows, decommit rules, and crediting for shortfalls; and (2) an oncall/escalation routing plan to handle reservation incidents and autoscale behaviors that cross SLAs.

Goals:
- Provide predictable commit windows for customers (start/end dates, committed throughput, and decommit windows).
- Make low-risk reservations fast to approve while keeping manual review for high-risk commitments.
- Ensure ops can quickly detect and remediate reservation-driven incidents (capacity hotspots, throttling, and autoscale failures).
- Integrate cost and commitment math into the reservation approval UI so sales/finance can review before signing.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Commit-window planner micro-spec: inputs (requested throughput, historical p95 usage, burst allowance), outputs (provision date, safe-commit delta, suggested pool assignment, billing schedule).
- Approval matrix rules: auto-approve thresholds, role-based manual approval lanes, SLA templates generated for each reservation.
- Decommit & crediting policy: grace periods, partial-decommit formulas, and customer crediting flow.
- Oncall routing spec: alert rules (Datadog), routing targets, escalation timeline, and post-incident playbook.
- UI changes: reservation detail page shows proposed commit window, risk score, cost estimate, and required approvals.
- Integrations: cost estimator (Finance), Dedicated fleet allocator (ENG), autoscale policy engine (ENG), and Console dashboards (Observability).

Decisions / Trade-offs:
- Auto-approve vs manual: we decided to auto-approve reservations under 10k RPS-equivalent or single-pool small commitments to reduce lead time. Anything above that requires manual review. Trade-off: shorter sales cycle vs operational risk.
- Conservative commit windows: we bias provision dates by +24–72 hours depending on fleet churn to avoid overpromising. This increases lead time but reduces rework.
- Canary reservations: for large commitments, we require a staged ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to catch model/runtime regressions before full commit. Adds complexity but materially reduces incidents.

Engineering Review Notes (summary):
- ENG concerns: autoscale policy needs a hard fallback to lower-capacity compatible model variants to avoid total outage; ENG-1842 will implement variant fallback.
- Capacity allocator: need new pool tagging for "reservation-canary" and "reservation-stable" to support staged rollouts (dependency ENG-19280).
- Runtime impact: KV-cache warmup windows will be exposed to the planner to calculate effective first-hour capacity loss.

Design Feedback:
- DES requested a compact risk score card for the reservation detail card: show three numbers (risk, lead-time, estimated monthly delta). Keep the CTA for manual approval prominent.

Security/Compliance:
- Security review flagged long-lived credentials when provisioning private on-prem fleets. Security review required before final approval (security_review_required = true).

Acceptance criteria (top-level):
- Commit-window planner returns deterministic windows for 95% of intake requests and aligns with allocator assignments.
- Auto-approval lane processes a simulated 200 requests/hour without false positives in the sandbox.
- Oncall routing triggers correct runbook within 2 minutes of a reservation-induced SLO breach in staging.
- Finance shows cost delta on reservation preview and approvals require explicit finance signoff for > $50k/month.

Success metrics:
- Time from reservation request to approval drops to < 48 hours for auto-eligible requests.
- Reduction in reservation-related incidents by 60% for new large customers after staged canary policy.
- Average overprovision delta (extra GPU minutes due to conservative windows) kept under 8% across Q2.

- PRD (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DED/pages/Reserve+Commit+Window+Planner
- Design mockups (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ReserveUI
- GitHub epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning/epics/commit-window-planner
- Allocator ticket (ENG): ENG-19280
- Autoscale policy RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/AutoscalePolicyRFC
- Staging dashboards (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/reservations/staging-v1

Open questions:
- Should we allow customers to pre-pay for shorter commit windows to speed provisioning? (Finance leaning yes; legal needs contract language.)
- How granular should canary bands be for multi-model fleets? (Default 10/50/100 vs model-specific ramping).

Next steps / Milestones:
- 2025-03-20: ENG first pass on allocator hooks (ENG-19280) -> done (see comments).
- 2025-03-28: Design signoff on reservation risk card -> in review.
- 2025-04-05: POC auto-approve lane in staging + load test.
- 2025-04-15: Ship beta to select customers with finance/legal approval.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on the edge cases in the decommit policy (partial decommits and prorated credits).
- Verify escalations integrate with the existing SRE oncall rotation (we'll map teams in ENG-1842).
